You are deleting one block from ONE Python file. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/identity_proposals.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                  (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## What to remove and why

Inside build_proposals there is a block, currently commented as a cross-source ambiguity veto, that iterates over the candidates routed to UNIPILE and calls the HubSpot client's search_by_name on each of them, collecting aliases into `cross_source_ambiguous`. That set is then consulted when a LinkedIn lookup finds no match, to relabel "no match" as ambiguous.

Delete it: the loop, the `cross_source_ambiguous` set, and the branch that reads it. When a LinkedIn search returns nothing, the reason is "no match".

The reason it must go is a disclosure rule, not a style preference. A cold candidate is routed to LinkedIn. Sending their name to HubSpot as well asks a second external system about a person for an answer that system was not asked for, and every name sent to a source is a disclosure. The file already honours this rule elsewhere: a candidate who already has an email address is skipped entirely rather than looked up. This block breaks the same rule for a different set of people.

It exists because of a defect in the checker, not because anything needed it. The checker's fixture planted two people sharing a name in HubSpot while routing that record to LinkedIn, so the only way to report the collision was to search HubSpot for LinkedIn-bound candidates. The fixture has been corrected — the ambiguous record is now warm and routes to HubSpot, where the collision actually is — and the checker now fails if any cold candidate's name reaches HubSpot at all.

## What must NOT change

Everything else in the file is verified and stays exactly as it is:

  * exactly one plausible match proposes; two or more propose nobody and record an ambiguity reason; zero records "no match";
  * a candidate who already has a usable email is never looked up anywhere;
  * every proposal carries evidence and a confidence;
  * nothing is applied, and no proposal is marked confirmed;
  * a source that raises is recorded reached=False with a one-line reason that leaks no credential or URL, returns no proposals, and does not stop the other source;
  * names are carried, intake note text is not;
  * the artifact is written atomically at mode 0600.

This is a deletion. Do not restructure the function, rename anything, or 'improve' neighbouring code.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u20_identity_proposals_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It currently fails with cold_disclosed_to_hubspot, naming how many HubSpot queries were made for candidates that do not route there.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what the loop now loses, if anything, by no longer cross-checking LinkedIn-bound names against HubSpot. Under 400 words.

The clean match, evidence, confidence, no-auto-apply, note-text, degraded-source and private-artifact assertions all still execute, so the disclosure fix cannot be bought by weakening anything else.
